subject: Velaris Dedicated Capacity: acceptance criteria & orchestration
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@velarisrx.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@velarisrx.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding - acceptance checklist request

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the hosted -> dedicated walkthrough yesterday. Velaris is excited to move ahead with a reserved pool for our production models. Before we lock dates, procurement needs a short, machine-readable acceptance checklist we can use for SRE sign-off. High level asks from our side:
- Validation criteria for throughput (p95 latency and sustained RPS)
- Required GPU types and whether prewarming is necessary
- How KV/prefix caching will be validated across canary traffic
- Expected blackout windows or risk windows for switchover

Attaching our current traffic matrix for the last 60 days so you can size against peak windows. Target go-live for business stakeholders is mid-November (ideally 2026-11-15) but we can be flexible if your team needs more runway.

Also, procurement asked whether SOC2 relevant artifacts can be referenced during the validation window — happy to share what they need.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Senior Engineering Manager
Velaris Therapeutics

Attachment: velaris_traffic_matrix_oct20.csv (CSV, 120 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@velarisrx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding - acceptance checklist request

Alex —

Appreciate the matrix, that helps a lot. I pushed an initial acceptance checklist draft and an orchestration outline to Ben (SE) for input; attaching the Redwood acceptance runbook v2 for your review. Highlights up front:
- Perf targets we validate against: p95 <= 220ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) on the committed GPU class; sustained throughput validated at your 75th-90th percentile RPS.
- Canary plan: 48-hour staging soak + 72-hour canary at 10% traffic, followed by a 24-hour ramp to 50% and then full shift if metrics hold.
- Required telemetry: token-level latency, error rate, GPU util, KV-hit ratio.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 degradation >25% OR error rate >1%.

Can Ben fill in exact GPU SKU recommendations and a short test script that your SREs can run?

I looped Ben in — Ben, can you add a quick checklist for model warmup and KV cache smoke tests?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_acceptance_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 430 KB)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding - acceptance checklist request

Alex / Kim —

Adding the SE perspective and a small tech acceptance checklist your SREs can run during staging. Summary:
1) GPU sizing
   - Baseline: 8x A100s (80GB) for current peak plus 30% headroom based on your matrix; recommend quantized weights if latency targets are strict.
2) Warmup / KV cache validation
   - Script: 3-phase warmup (cold load -> steady run 30m -> KV-hit verification). I attached a short shell snippet in the runbook.
3) Throughput smoke tests
   - 15-minute p95/p99 sampling at target RPS, compare against hosted baseline.
4) Canary traffic orchestration
   - Canary slice: route 10% of traffic using header x-velaris-canary; verify stable GPU util and KV hit ratio for 72 hrs before ramping.
5) Safety nets
   - Auto-fallback: Redwood will keep a hosted fallback model in the routing policy for the first 7 days post shift.

Operational notes:
- If you expect bursts >2x baseline for short windows, add burst capacity flag in the commit so we can provision ephemeral nodes.
- We'll need a list of model SHAs and any custom ops you use (FFN kernels) so we can pre-validate compilation paths.

I attached the small SE runbook snippets to the runbook. Happy to run the warmup script with your SREs in a joint session.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben / Kim — this is exactly the detail I needed. A few follow-ups from our side:
- Procurement reviewed the runbook; they asked for the blackout/maintenance windows to be called out explicitly (we cannot have any shifts during our nightly batch windows: 02:00–03:30 PT).
- Confirmed go-live target: 2026-11-15, but we need the canary to start no earlier than 2026-11-08 to allow calendar approvals.
- SOC2: attaching a short excerpt procurement requested to cross-check logs/retention for the staging window.

One operational ask: can Redwood provide a short post-shift validation checklist (10–12 checks) that our on-call can run within the first 4 hours after full shift? That would help us sign-off faster.

Alex Morgan
Senior Engineering Manager, Velaris Therapeutics

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity onboarding - acceptance checklist request 

Alex / Priya —

Attached is an orchestration timeline that maps directly to the items we discussed and includes the 12-point post-shift validation for your on-call. Key dates and windows (proposed):
- 2026-11-02: Staging activation (48-hour soak) — internal validation by Velaris SREs and Redwood SEs.
- 2026-11-08: Canary start (10% traffic) — 72-hour stable window. No canary before this date per your ask.
- 2026-11-12: Ramp to 50% (24 hours) then 100% shift on 2026-11-13 if metrics pass. If you prefer business date 2026-11-15 as final acceptance, we can schedule 11/13 for shift and hold until your exec sign-off on 11/15.
- Blackout window respected: No shifts between 02:00–03:30 PT.

Operational commitments from Redwood:
- Warmup script & run with your SREs during staging (Ben to lead).
- Continuous telemetry dashboard shared (token-latency, errors, GPU util) for the full validation period.
- Hosted fallback remains live for 7 days after shift.

Next steps: please review the orchestration plan and confirm (a) acceptance of the suggested dates, and (b) the list of model SHAs by 2026-11-01 so Ben can pre-validate compilation. Once you confirm, I will create the HubSpot deal task and a DocuSign PO for the reserved capacity commitment.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint run.

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
